title: Genome-wide mapping of RNA-protein associations through sequencing
boundary: SMART-display protein labels and the REILIS module convert protein-associated RNAs into linked protein-label/RNA DNA read pairs. The biochemical boundary is a genome-scale protein-label library coupled to RNA/cDNA proximity ligation, rather than an antibody panel expansion or ordinary RNA-protein immunoprecipitation.
evidence_scope: Published Nature Biotechnology9Sep2025 identity/abstract and ExtendedData1–2 overview verified in indexed primary article; issue44:1202–1212 is2026. Author GEO GSE270010 independently describes the two modules. Direct Nature open redirected to inaccessible identity endpoint. PMC11398515 is superseded preprint10.1101/2024.09.04.611288; checked identity only, not adopted as published recipe. No full Methods/SI or correction audit.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of cytoplasmic RBP-RNA interactions and transcriptome in living cells by engineered protein nanocages
boundary: RBP-fused EPN24 nanocages package selected cellular RNAs into secreted particles; clarified culture-supernatant recovery feeds sequencing without destroying the source cell population. Engineered secretion and physical extracellular RNA recovery distinguish this preparation from CLIP/RIP or intracellular RNA-editing tagging; individual RBP or cell-type applications remain one method.
evidence_scope: Published Molecular Cell2026 identity/summary, Design andFig1A–B workflow accessible in indexed primary publisher text;16Jul2026issue86:2871–2887.e8. Primary PubMed42349405 and author BioProjectPRJNA1247426 support identity/overview. No full Methods/SI, construct sequence or correction/version-comparison audit; no secondary highlight used as chemistry authority.

title: Resolving cell–cell interaction networks and their molecular logic in complex tissues
boundary: Partially dissociated native cell clumps receive membrane-anchored oligos and three split-pool ligation rounds before complete dissociation and droplet RNA/index-library capture. Physical clump-level molecular indexing precedes single-cell indexing, unlike ProximID paired-cell sorting, routine sample hashing or computational interaction prediction.
evidence_scope: Published Nature Methods5Oct2026 identity, abstract and Results Accurate identification of cell–cell interactions by CCI-seq/Fig1 overview verified in primary indexed article. Author OMIX016046 confirms same-work identity; not counted separately. No whole Methods/SI, primer transcription or correction audit; predecessor component/version review remains pending.

title: Spatial chromatin architecture and accessibility co-profiling of mammalian tissues
boundary: In-tissue proximity ligation precedes Tn5 fragmentation of contact DNA, then orthogonal microfluidic barcode ligations and biotin-fragment enrichment. This changed on-slide substrate/order and barcode-installation boundary adds spatial contact/accessibility readout beyond HiCAR or ordinary spatial ATAC; neither tissue substitution nor array resolution alone establishes distinction.
evidence_scope: Published Nature Methods1Sep2026 identity, Results Development/Fig1 overview and selected primary protocol overview accessible; Octoberissue23:2015–2028. Both modalities derive from the contact-library workflow rather than an assumed independent RNA library. Full SI/oligo/end/physical-fraction curation and correction/version audit remain unperformed.

title: Nanopore sequencing of intact aminoacylated tRNAs
boundary: Chemical ligation uses an activated RNA adapter to retain an amino acid between charged tRNA and adapter, followed by nanopore sequencing of the adapted molecule. Preserving the aminoacyl bridge changes the covalent substrate/read-through interface relative to deacylated tRNA sequencing or generic polyadenylation; no new tRNA target panel is counted.
evidence_scope: Published Nature Communications20Aug2025 identity and primary abstract/chemical-ligation Results overview verified; article16:7781, publishedPMCIDPMC12368100. Direct HTML open redirected to inaccessible identity endpoint, while indexed published HTML/PDF overview is available. Supersededpreprint10.1101/2024.11.18.623114/PMC11601438 checked for identity only; no preprint recipe or full Methods/SI/correction audit.

title: Defining expansions and perturbations to the RNA polymerase III transcriptome and epitranscriptome by modified direct RNA nanopore sequencing
boundary: Subtract poly(A)+ RNA and rRNA, ligate a poly(U)-targeting nanopore adapter, synthesize protective cDNA, and digest remaining unadapted single-stranded RNA before motor-adapter finishing. Adapter-end recognition plus nuclease-protected enrichment is a different preparation from generic direct RNA or mature-tRNA sequencing, beyond a new PolIII gene panel.
